UD-001.notes: Cool grey blocks, worn edges and dust at the floor; intact wall and reverse masonry stay stone.

UD-002.notes: Raised bones above the measured 14.35 mm floor crest; the irregular wall front is excluded at x=9.9 mm.

UD-003.notes: All skulls and long bones in front of the wall receive aged ivory; floor joints and irregular wall remain stone.

UD-004.notes: Two vertical bars inside the measured arched opening are dark iron; arched surround, sill and walls remain grey masonry.

UD-005.notes: Floor skull plus two skulls on the broken sill; sill bones above z=31.25 mm are isolated from the two arch piers.

UD-007.notes: Shackles and chain protrusions in front of x=9.9 mm and above the stone floor receive dark iron, gentle wear and PBR metal response.

UD-008.notes: Broken masonry and fallen pieces retain cold stone; raised rubble is a little lighter and dustier than the standing piers.

UD-011.notes: Reuse measured UD-010 door parts, with the rounded iron inspection-window frame and vertical bars at y=-7.4..7.4, z=42.95..55.55 mm; vertical aged wood grain remains on both sides.

UD-012.notes: Both opposing walls and cobbles are cool masonry; consistent edge wear and recessed floor mortar.

UD-014.notes: Both walls, exposed brick caps and the irregular floor remain stone; light wear follows the actual geometry.

UD-015.notes: Outer ring, worn lip and inner shaft remain cold stone; no invented water in the empty well.

UD-016.notes: Irregular pavers, lighter worn crests and darker recessed mortar; preserve the thin floor datum.

UD-017.notes: Large and small pavers remain separate, with cold grain and visibly recessed mortar.

UD-018.notes: Stone around the broken hole, worn fracture edges and dark recessed joints; the shaft remains open.
